sampling_model.design: The design deterministically selects one proxy intervention set \(A\subseteq V\setminus\{s\}\) and acquires \(Q[V\setminus A]=P(V\setminus A\mid\operatorname{do}(A))\). Feasibility means identification of \(Q_s\) from that law under the cited hedge criterion; finite-sample allocation is outside scope.
sampling_model.units: Vertices of the fixed finite observed ADMG \(G\) induced by a recursive semi-Markovian structural causal model.
sampling_model.treatment: Acquisition of the proxy interventional law produced by intervening on the selected vertices \(A\).
sampling_model.overlap: Identification is interpreted uniformly over positive recursive semi-Markovian models compatible with \(G\), exactly as in the imported convention. This semantic positivity is separate from bow-freeness, hedge rank, costs, approximation, and vertex orders.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None; the target is experiment acquisition sufficient for graphical identification, not estimation from finite samples.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Appendix D.2 gives polynomial optimization when every minimal hedge residual has size at most two, while fixed larger size only makes enumeration polynomial and leaves hitting set exponential.
Theorems 1--2 encode MCID feasibility as SAT and then WPMAX-SAT or ILP, and the conclusion leaves efficient approximation as future work.
Theorem 6 and Corollaries 2--3 make hedges complete graphical witnesses for failure of interventional identification.
Optimal fractional vertex-packing solutions have half-integral basic optima and their integral coordinates persist in an integral optimum.
Theorem 3.1 establishes APX-completeness of minimum vertex cover on cubic graphs.
Assuming the Unique Games Conjecture, minimum vertex cover has no polynomial approximation factor below two.
The vertex-cover LP integrality gap on a graph is \(2-2/\chi^f(G)\).
Weighted \(d\)-Hitting Set with an explicit hyperedge list admits parameterized search-tree algorithms.

body.tldr: Under the standard positive-compatible recursive semi-Markovian semantics, acquiring \(Q[V\setminus A]=P(V\setminus A\mid\operatorname{do}(A))\) identifies the causal target \(Q_s\) exactly when \(A\) hits every minimal residual hedge. Rank three is the first nonzero minimal residual-hedge rank for finite simple bow-free singleton-target ADMGs, and four-vertex hedges are exactly complementary directed and bidirected spanning paths. A one-private-guard expansion realizes every finite graph edge clutter and yields unit-cost \(\mathsf{NP}\)- and \(\mathsf{APX}\)-hardness on radius-two bidirected trees. Under \(r(G,s)\leq3\), exact promised enumeration and parent-spouse thresholding give a weighted factor-two algorithm; complete-graph expansions show that the natural-LP gap supremum is two, and the \(\mathsf{UGC}\)-conditional \((2-\epsilon)\) lower bound transfers to the unit-cost radius-two-tree subclass. Every polynomial-time assertion is made on the canonical \(\mathrm{Fin}\,n\)-encoded carrier, with polynomial rational bit complexity and guarded composition, and then transferred to a generic finite supplied-ordered carrier by relabeling invariance. The optimizer-or-rank-violation interface does not claim unrestricted rank recognition or unconstrained weighted \(3^k\) optimization.

project_justification.gap: The published minimum-cost intervention-design frontier jumps from polynomial solvability at residual size two to unrestricted logarithmic hardness, but it does not identify the first nonempty finite simple bow-free singleton-target rank, the exact weighted natural-LP gap at that boundary, or the approximation threshold on a graphically sparse hard subclass.
project_justification.niche: Rank-three hedge clutters are not arbitrary three-uniform clutters: every minimal residual crosses the target-parent and target-spouse partition. This structure controls every positive-rational-cost instance under the rank promise, while private guards still realize every graph edge clutter inside the narrower unit-cost class whose bidirected graph is a radius-two tree.
project_justification.fill: The paper imports the positive-compatible recursive semi-Markovian hedge-hitting identification bridge, then proves the four-vertex obstruction classification, exact private-guard realization, objective-preserving hardness, and the exact weighted natural-LP gap two at promised rank three. Source expansions use an order \(\prec\) on \(U\), while promised enumeration uses a distinct causal-vertex order \(\triangleleft_V\) on \(V\). All algorithmic and reduction maps are stated first on the canonical \(\mathrm{Fin}\,n\)-encoded carrier with binary rational costs; elementary graph and rational operations and guarded compositions have polynomial cost there, and relabeling invariance transfers the outputs and objective guarantees to arbitrary finite supplied-ordered carriers. Complete-graph gadgets provide the matching gap sequence, the \(\mathsf{UGC}\)-conditional \((2-\epsilon)\) threshold holds on the narrower unit-cost radius-two-tree subclass, and the bounded-cardinality and optimizer-or-violation interfaces retain their promised scope.

body.related_work: Richardson and Spirtes supply the finite simple ADMG and bow-free conventions. Shpitser and Pearl provide the complete hedge obstruction, and Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash give its positive-compatible proxy-intervention formulation and the minimum-weight hedge-hitting program. They prove unrestricted hardness and polynomial solvability through residual size two; this paper establishes the first nonempty bow-free singleton boundary and its rank-three approximation frontier. Elahi and coauthors' RC2 and Gurobi formulations are direct computational consumers. Alimonti and Kann supply cubic Vertex Cover \(\mathsf{APX}\)-completeness, Khot and Regev supply the \(\mathsf{UGC}\)-conditional factor-two graph threshold, and Korte and Vygen supply rational linear-programming in polynomial input time. Those imported complexity statements are used on the canonical \(\mathrm{Fin}\,n\)-encoded carrier fixed here; relabeling invariance, polynomial rational bit complexity, and closure under guarded composition transfer the resulting algorithms and reductions to generic finite supplied-ordered carriers. Singh's source LP-gap formula is only motivation for the independently proved complete-graph calculation, and Fernau's branching result informs only the scoped cardinality-bounded search. No unrestricted rank-three recognizer is claimed.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The factor-two algorithm is promise-based: polynomial enumeration is guaranteed only after \(r(G,s)\leq3\) and a causal-vertex order \(\triangleleft_V\) on \(V\) are supplied, and a successful optimizer run does not certify the rank bound. The order \(\triangleleft_V\) controls only lexicographic output and differs from the source order \(\prec\). The \(O(3^k)\) exact-search guarantee requires a supplied cardinality bound \(k\). Polynomial time means polynomial in \(n\) and the canonical binary encoding length \(L\) on the \(\mathrm{Fin}\,n\) carrier; transfer to a generic finite type requires its supplied order and the declared relabeling invariance. Finite-sample allocation and statistical estimation remain outside this combinatorial identification-design result.
body.honest_scope: The causal bridge is imported under positive-compatible recursive semi-Markovian semantics; no finite-sample or weaker-positivity extension is claimed. The exact weighted gap supremum covers positive-rational-cost finite simple bow-free singleton-target instances with \(r(G,s)\leq3\) and nonempty clutter, whereas the matching hardness subclass has unit costs and a radius-two bidirected tree. Every polynomial-time map is interpreted on the canonical \(\mathrm{Fin}\,n\)-encoded adjacency-and-cost representation and transferred to a generic finite supplied-ordered carrier only through relabeling invariance; rational field operations are charged at binary bit complexity and guarded compositions remain polynomial. The source order \(\prec\) and causal enumeration order \(\triangleleft_V\) are distinct. Rank-at-most-three recognition, planar realizability, rank-four realizability, finite-sample allocation, and solver speedups remain open, and weighted \(O(3^k)\) search is asserted only with a supplied cardinality bound.
